matchstick.title: Compute numeric values and discrepancy
matchstick.principle: Before moving any stick, calculate the integer values of both sides of the equation and determine the numeric discrepancy; this guides which stick moves could potentially balance the equation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after parsing the equation, before enumerating any stick moves.
matchstick.example: Proceeding to move sticks without first noting that XV = 15 and XV + XV = 30, leading to moves that don't address the 15‑unit gap.

matchstick.title: List possible single‑stick transformations
matchstick.principle: Systematically enumerate every way a single matchstick can be moved, considering all possible source characters (including operators) and all valid target placements, to generate candidate moves.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After computing the discrepancy, generate the full set of candidate stick relocations.
matchstick.example: Only considering moves that change one numeral to another, while ignoring the possibility of moving a stick within the same operator.

matchstick.title: Match numeric difference to value change
matchstick.principle: For each candidate stick move, compute how the move changes the numeric values of the affected numerals and operators, and keep only moves that can bridge the computed discrepancy.
matchstick.when_to_apply: During evaluation of each candidate transformation.
matchstick.example: Choosing a transformation that changes XV to XIV (−1) when the equation requires a change of +15.

matchstick.title: Consider intra‑character repositioning
matchstick.principle: Allow a stick to be moved within the same character, changing its orientation or position to transform the character into another valid numeral or operator (e.g., turning V into X, or '+' into '=' by repositioning a stick).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When enumerating candidate moves, include repositioning a stick inside its own character.
matchstick.example: Overlooking the option to reposition the vertical stick of '+' to become a horizontal, thus missing the conversion of '+' into '='.

matchstick.title: Operator modification via equals
matchstick.principle: Treat the '=' sign as two horizontal sticks; moving one of its sticks can turn it into a '-' sign, and the removed stick can be placed elsewhere to adjust values.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When evaluating operator transformations, consider converting '=' to '-' by removing a horizontal stick.
matchstick.example: Attempting to turn '=' into '≠' by adding a vertical stick, which is prohibited.

matchstick.title: Operator modification via plus
matchstick.principle: A '+' consists of one vertical and one horizontal stick; removing the vertical stick converts it into a '-' sign, while the removed vertical stick can be placed elsewhere to adjust numerals.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When evaluating operator transformations, consider converting '+' to '-' by removing its vertical stick.
matchstick.example: Failing to move the vertical stick from '+' to the left 'I', missing the solution that creates '-' and augments 'I' to 'II'.

matchstick.title: Inter‑character stick relocation
matchstick.principle: When moving a stick, allow it to be taken from any character (numeral or operator) and placed onto a different character, provided both source and target remain valid after the move.
matchstick.when_to_apply: During enumeration of candidate moves, include moves that relocate a stick across characters.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick from '+' to 'I' but forgetting to verify that '+' remains a valid operator after losing the vertical stick.

matchstick.title: Operator‑to‑operator stick relocation
matchstick.principle: A stick can be moved directly from one operator to another, simultaneously changing both operators (e.g., turning '+' into '-' while turning '=' into '-'), as long as each remains a valid operator after the move.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When considering moves that involve two operators, evaluate the combined effect on both.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick from '+' to '=', resulting in an invalid combination such as '≠' or leaving one operator without the required sticks.

matchstick.title: Source character must stay valid after stick removal
matchstick.principle: Before moving a stick, ensure that the source character can lose that stick and still represent a valid Roman numeral or operator; otherwise the move is illegal.
matchstick.when_to_apply: During candidate generation, filter out moves that would leave the source character invalid.
matchstick.example: Removing a diagonal from 'X', leaving a single diagonal line that does not correspond to any Roman numeral.

matchstick.description: Leaving a character invalid after moving a stick
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on numeric impact and forgets the syntactic validity of characters.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Check that each character still matches a known Roman numeral or operator after the stick is removed.

matchstick.description: Failing to verify numeric equality after transformation
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model assumes any syntactically correct equation is acceptable, neglecting the numeric evaluation.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After applying a stick move, recompute the values of both sides and confirm equality.

matchstick.description: Dropping or omitting parts of the equation
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model truncates the output or forgets to include all tokens after a transformation.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Ensure the final answer contains the same structural components (including an equality sign) as the original, unless a valid transformation explicitly changes them.

matchstick.description: Attempting to change '=' into an invalid operator
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model treats any operator change as permissible without recalling the rule against '≠'.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Remember that '=' may only become '-' by losing a horizontal stick; it must never become '≠' or disappear.

matchstick.description: Ignoring the numeric impact of operator sign change
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on character validity and overlooks the effect of operator changes on the equation's value.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When modifying an operator, recalculate the expression's numeric result to ensure the change moves toward equality.
